concepts.def: Young British Artists active from the late 1990s.
Borrowing existing images into new artworks.
Idea is the artwork, more than the object.

walkthroughs.body_html: Pop Art rose in Britain and America in the 1950s-60s. Andy Warhol screen-printed Marilyn Monroe and Campbell's soup cans; Roy Lichtenstein imitated comic book dots. It blurred the line between fine art and advertising.

From around 1990, the YBAs — including Damien Hirst, Tracey Emin and Sarah Lucas — became famous through the Sensation exhibition (1997). They used shock, autobiography and installation to challenge what art could be.

Conceptual art, traced to artists like Sol LeWitt and Yoko Ono, treats the idea itself as the artwork. Today's contemporary practice is plural — performance, video, digital, social practice — often crossing several of these traditions at once.
